plan.title: Melanoma anti-PD-1 immune/stromal composition from TPM
plan.analytical_narrative: The core delivered only a gene-level TPM table (12000 genes x 12 samples) from Salmon, no raw counts, so any count-based model (DESeq2/edgeR) is invalid; the plan follows the TPM branch throughout: log2(TPM+1) for QC and any linear modeling, no count-style normalization. Sample sample_01 runs at ~1/4 median depth — it is kept, inspected on PCA/library-size plots, and only dropped with a stated reason if it proves to be an outlier, per rule R-0008. The research question is composition, not DE, so no differential expression step is included (avoiding unasked scope): Track 1 does sample structure QC and the low-abundance filter needed before any TPM-based inference; Track 2 runs the deconvolution itself. Because CIBERSORT/LM22 and ESTIMATE are proprietary and absent from this environment, EPIC and quanTIseq (open, TPM-native, return absolute fractions with an uncharacterized/other fraction) are the primary methods, run through the immunedeconv common interface; MCP-counter (semi-quantitative abundance scores) and xCell (64-type enrichment scores with spillover compensation) are added as cross-checks so that any composition claim rests on agreement across >=2 methods (R-0128), not one tool's numbers. Group comparison is a t-test per cell type/method on n=6 vs n=6 with BH correction across the tested types, following R-0134 (a score is one value per sample, so the DE replicate count applies, not the gene count). The final report states which claims are consensus (>=2 methods agree in direction) versus single-method observations, and explicitly separates EPIC/quanTIseq 'proportion' semantics from xCell/MCP-counter 'enrichment score' semantics so the two are never treated as the same unit. No count-based DE, no ESTIMATE purity claim, and no CIBERSORT/LM22 claim are made anywhere in this plan, consistent with what tooling is actually available.

EPIC absolute cell fractions via immunedeconv, quanTIseq and MCP-counter as cross-checks, xCell for broader stromal/immune enrichment
